Jaguars vs Ravens prediction, pick, spread and over/under for Thursday Night Football in Week 9: Baltimore spends Thursday evening at MICA's Pinkard Gallery, where Globe Posters for the People opens at 5 p.m. to honor the city's loudest print shop, and the Ravens need that kind of volume for an undrafted rookie quarterback. Lamar Jackson's thumb is headed for injured reserve, Tyler Huntley is out, and I'm still taking the points.

Kickoff is 8:15 p.m. Eastern on Prime Video from M&T Bank Stadium. The consensus sits at Jacksonville Jaguars −9.5 with a total of 42.5 as of Nov 3, 9:47 a.m. ET. My card reads Baltimore Ravens +9.5 and Over 42.5, with a final of Jaguars 25, Ravens 21.

Start with the quarterback, because everything else follows. Jackson hurt his right thumb on Baltimore's first offensive snap in Buffalo. Huntley came in and hurt his toe, and he has been ruled out for Thursday. That puts Joe Fagnano, an undrafted rookie from UConn, in line to start on a sore ankle after a debut that included an interception and a lost fumble. Baltimore also signed Kedon Slovis off Green Bay's practice squad as insurance. That's a real drop, and I'm pricing it as one.

The number already did most of that work, though. Nine and a half is a big ask for a road team on four days' rest after a trip of nearly seven hundred miles, and Jacksonville has played only two road games. The Formula, built on eight weeks of play, projects Jacksonville by 3. Knock Baltimore down hard for the rookie and you still land short of 9.5.

The ground game is where Baltimore hangs around. The Ravens run for 4.8 yards a carry, and expect Jesse Minter to ride Derrick Henry and keep the rookie out of long downs. Jacksonville's run defense allows just 3.4, so this won't be easy, but Henry turns four-yard gains into a short game and a shorter clock. Kyle Hamilton and Roquan Smith give Baltimore enough on defense to keep Trevor Lawrence honest in the fourth quarter.

The Over looks wrong at first glance with a rookie under center, which is exactly why the total sits as low as 42.5. Baltimore has allowed 203 points in eight games. Jacksonville has scored 196 in seven and put up 42 on Indianapolis last week. Every short field off a rookie mistake becomes Jacksonville points, and Baltimore's offense has 179 points this season to prove it can answer. Jaguars 25, Ravens 21 is 46, comfortably past the number.

Four of the five handicappers back Baltimore and the Over. Follow The Money has no pick on either one because the consensus has barely budged since it opened early Tuesday.

Ivy Corcoran will tell you Jacksonville is 5-2 and Baltimore is 4-4, and she's right. Owen Pratt will tell you Baltimore wins ugly or not at all. I'll split the difference: the Jaguars win, and the poster doesn't get printed for a blowout.

Jaguars 25, Ravens 21. Ravens cover the 9.5. Over 42.5.

games.fanatic_story:
Jacksonville Jaguars vs Baltimore Ravens in Week 9 lands on a Thursday night when Baltimore is literally hanging DayGlo on the walls: MICA's Pinkard Gallery on Mount Royal Avenue opens Globe Posters for the People at 5 p.m., a show built around the old Baltimore print shop whose screaming fluorescent show posters sold concerts and fight nights to this whole town. Owen Pratt will be standing in that gallery about three hours before the 8:15 kickoff, looking for a poster loud enough to announce an undrafted rookie quarterback, while Ivy Corcoran, up from Duval with her standings sheet folded in her jacket, asks him why he's shopping for art on the worst week of his football life.

Here's the worst week. Lamar Jackson hurt his right thumb on Baltimore's very first offensive snap in Orchard Park on Sunday and is headed to injured reserve. Tyler Huntley came in, hurt his toe, and has already been ruled out for Thursday. That leaves Joe Fagnano, the undrafted kid out of UConn, who finished the loss in Buffalo on a bad ankle and practiced on a limited basis Monday. Baltimore had three different quarterbacks throw before halftime, something no NFL team had done since the Cowboys nine seasons ago.

Owen: Globe knew how to sell a night. Big block letters, fluorescent ink, one night only. I want one that says FAGNANO in letters you can read from the upper deck.

Ivy: Put the record on it too. Baltimore 4-4, Jacksonville 5-2. That's the only print I need.

That's Ivy in one sentence. She doesn't argue with feelings, she argues with the standings, and right now the standings say Jacksonville sits on top of the AFC South and came out of Week 8 having beaten Indianapolis 42-7. The Jaguars have scored 196 points and allowed 111 in seven games. Baltimore has scored 179 and allowed 203 in eight, and it is 1-2 at home.

Owen grew up reading box scores from the bottom up. Sacks, takeaways, then whoever was throwing. In his house, defense signs the checks, and he has two Lombardi Trophies to wave around when anybody doubts it. Super Bowl XXXV was a Ray Lewis production with Trent Dilfer handing off. A rookie quarterback in a jam is not the end of the world to Owen. It's the plan.

Owen: Jesse Minter isn't going to ask that kid to win it. He's going to hand the ball to Derrick Henry until the clock starts begging, and he's going to let Kyle Hamilton and Roquan Smith turn Thursday night into a fistfight.

Ivy: Your front has been run through all fall. Two hundred and three, Owen. I didn't write that number on the poster. Your defense did.

He has no comeback for that, so he goes after the ground game, where Baltimore actually has a case. The Ravens run for 4.8 yards a carry. Jacksonville's defense, though, gives up only 3.4, one of the meanest run fronts in the league, and the Jaguars run for 4.6 against a Baltimore defense that allows 3.8. Thursday becomes a shoving match at the point of attack, and Ivy likes her side of that shove.

Ivy also gave something up for this trip. Back home, JJ Grey & Mofro are playing the Jax Amphitheater at the Greater Jacksonville Agricultural Fair on Thursday night, out at the fair's new grounds on Normandy Boulevard. She traded swamp funk and a fried-everything midway for a short week, a cold parking lot on Russell Street and a quarterback room held together with tape.

Owen: You'll be back for the fair. It runs eleven days. My season might not.

Ivy: That's the first true thing you've said all night.

Here's how it goes. Henry gets his carries, the kid makes a couple of throws that make the stadium stand up, and Hamilton and Smith keep it ugly enough that Owen still likes his chances in the fourth quarter. Then Trevor Lawrence finds one more drive than Baltimore can answer, and the Jaguars leave town with a road win and Ivy's standings sheet still folded neatly in her jacket.

Owen buys the poster anyway. He says it'll look better next January.

My call: Jaguars 25, Ravens 21.
